cards.title: Laundromat at Midnight
cards.prompt: A laundromat at midnight. One dryer has been thumping for an hour.
cards.tip: Decide whose laundry is in that dryer.

cards.title: Motel Ice Machine
cards.prompt: A motel ice-machine alcove. The machine groans like it has opinions.
cards.tip: Start mid-errand. Why does someone need ice now?

cards.title: Lighthouse Stairs
cards.prompt: Halfway up a lighthouse staircase. Wind whistles through a cracked window.
cards.tip: Say how many steps are left.

cards.title: Bowling Shoe Counter
cards.prompt: The shoe counter at a bowling alley. It smells of disinfectant spray.
cards.tip: Name a shoe size in your first line.

cards.title: Dentist’s Waiting Room
cards.prompt: A dentist’s waiting room. The fish tank bubbles louder than it should.
cards.tip: Waiting rooms make everyone polite. Use that.

cards.title: Lawn Chairs on the Moon
cards.prompt: Two lawn chairs on the moon. It is silent and very dusty.
cards.tip: Play it like a normal picnic that happens in space.

cards.title: Stuck Ferris Wheel
cards.prompt: The top of a stopped Ferris wheel. The car creaks when anyone shifts.
cards.tip: You are perfectly safe. Describe the view out loud.

cards.title: Gate 99
cards.prompt: Gate 99 at 4 a.m. The carpet smells of coffee and patience.
cards.tip: Name the destination in your first two lines.

cards.title: Backstage, One Minute
cards.prompt: Backstage at a school play. The curtain smells of dust and hairspray.
cards.tip: Something is missing. Treat it as a puzzle.

cards.title: Lost and Found
cards.prompt: A theme park lost-and-found at closing. Somewhere, a toy keeps squeaking.
cards.tip: Name one lost thing and who misses it.

cards.title: Submarine Galley
cards.prompt: The galley of a submarine. A sonar ping sounds every few seconds.
cards.tip: Cook something specific in a very small space.

cards.title: Middle of the Maze
cards.prompt: The centre of a hedge maze. It smells of cut grass and sunscreen.
cards.tip: Agree early on how long you’ve been lost.

cards.title: Inside the Car Wash
cards.prompt: Inside a car wash, mid-cycle. The brushes thunder across the roof.
cards.tip: You have exactly one cycle to sort something out.

cards.title: Greenhouse in Winter
cards.prompt: A greenhouse in winter. The air is warm, wet and smells of tomatoes.
cards.tip: Name the plant you are proudest of.

cards.title: Museum After Hours
cards.prompt: A dinosaur museum after closing. Every footstep echoes off the bones.
cards.tip: Decide in two lines why you’re allowed in.

cards.title: The Cheese Cave
cards.prompt: A cheese cave dug into a hillside. It smells exactly as you’d fear.
cards.tip: Name a cheese. Invent one if you need to.

cards.title: The Long Escalator
cards.prompt: A very long escalator going down. Every third step squeaks.
cards.tip: Nothing to do but talk. Make the ride matter.

cards.title: The Quiet Carriage
cards.prompt: The quiet carriage of a train. Every crunch of a snack is enormous.
cards.tip: Whisper. Let the urgency grow as the voices shrink.

cards.title: Treehouse in a Storm
cards.prompt: A treehouse in a rainstorm. The roof drums, and one corner drips.
cards.tip: Decide whose treehouse it is and what it’s for.

cards.title: Balloon Basket
cards.prompt: A hot-air balloon basket. The burner roars every few seconds.
cards.tip: Name what’s below you in your first line.

cards.title: Bakery at 4 a.m.
cards.prompt: A bakery kitchen at 4 a.m. Warm bread, and flour in the air.
cards.tip: Something must be baked before the doors open.

cards.title: Indoor Pool
cards.prompt: An indoor swimming pool. Every word echoes, and it smells of chlorine.
cards.tip: Decide early: in the water, or beside it?

cards.title: Canoe in the Fog
cards.prompt: A canoe on a foggy lake. Paddles drip; a loon calls somewhere.
cards.tip: You can only hear the shore. Describe the sounds.

cards.title: Parking Garage, Level 9
cards.prompt: Level 9 of a parking garage. A car alarm chirps, politely, somewhere.
cards.tip: Nobody remembers where they parked. Build the search.

cards.title: Petting Zoo
cards.prompt: A petting zoo at feeding time. Goats bleat, and the hay itches.
cards.tip: Give one goat a name and a reputation.

cards.title: Desert Rest Stop
cards.prompt: A desert rest stop at noon. The vending machine hums in the heat.
cards.tip: One thing in that machine is very important.

cards.title: Stay With the Group
cards.prompt: A tour guide who needs you to stay with the group, please, this time.
cards.tip: Treat one ordinary thing as a famous landmark.

cards.title: Retired Superhero
cards.prompt: A retired superhero who needs you to admit they’ve still got it.
cards.tip: Name your old power. It has shrunk with age.

cards.title: From Next Tuesday
cards.prompt: A time traveller from next Tuesday who must stop you eating that sandwich.
cards.tip: Never explain why. Just get more urgent.

cards.title: One More Cup
cards.prompt: A lighthouse keeper who needs you to stay for one more cup of tea.
cards.tip: Find a new, smaller reason each time.

cards.title: Very New Intern
cards.prompt: A brand-new intern who needs you to approve every tiny decision they make.
cards.tip: Ask permission for things nobody asks permission for.

cards.title: Roll Call
cards.prompt: A substitute teacher who needs you to prove your name is really your name.
cards.tip: Stay polite. Get more suspicious with each answer.

cards.title: Vegetarian Dragon
cards.prompt: A dragon on a strict vegetarian diet who needs you to hide the sausages.
cards.tip: Proud of the diet. Weak near sausages.

cards.title: Forty Years Overdue
cards.prompt: A librarian who needs you to return a book that’s forty years overdue.
cards.tip: Never raise your voice. Name the book.

cards.title: Sacred Errand
cards.prompt: A knight on a sacred quest who needs you to sell them one stamp.
cards.tip: Treat the small thing like a holy relic.

cards.title: Undercover Royal
cards.prompt: A royal in disguise who needs you to treat them like a normal customer.
cards.tip: A royal habit keeps slipping out.

cards.title: Hurt GPS
cards.prompt: A car’s GPS with feelings who needs you to admit you ignored its turn.
cards.tip: Give directions that are really life advice.

cards.title: Bored Detective
cards.prompt: A detective with no cases who needs you to be guilty of something, anything.
cards.tip: Investigate a fact everyone already knows.

cards.title: Stay Very Calm
cards.prompt: A beekeeper who needs you to stay very, very calm right now.
cards.tip: Speak softly and slowly. Never quite say why.

cards.title: Step Back, Please
cards.prompt: A museum guard who needs you to step back from the painting. Further.
cards.tip: Treat every inch as a serious rule.

cards.title: Pigeon With a Speech
cards.prompt: A pigeon who needs you to share your chips, and has prepared a speech.
cards.tip: Use big formal words. Never forget the chips.

cards.title: Imaginary Friend
cards.prompt: A seven-year-old’s imaginary friend who needs you to finally believe in them.
cards.tip: Prove you’re real with very specific memories.

cards.title: Robot Vacuum
cards.prompt: A robot vacuum who needs you to lift your feet. Again.
cards.tip: Stay flat and patient. Report every crumb.

cards.title: The Last Potato
cards.prompt: A grandparent who needs you to take the last potato, no arguments.
cards.tip: Every refusal earns a better reason to eat it.

cards.title: Short on Teeth
cards.prompt: A tooth fairy who needs to borrow one of your teeth; they’re short this week.
cards.tip: Treat it like a perfectly normal business loan.

cards.title: It Is Raining
cards.prompt: A weather forecaster who needs you to agree it’s raining. It isn’t.
cards.tip: Report the weather calmly, like it’s the news.

cards.title: Name the Ingredient
cards.prompt: A chef who needs you to taste the soup and name the secret ingredient.
cards.tip: React to every wrong guess like it’s a clue.

cards.title: Check Your Pockets
cards.prompt: A magician whose trick went wrong, who needs you to check your pockets.
cards.tip: Name what was supposed to appear.

cards.title: Forgot the Password
cards.prompt: A spy who needs you to say the password, which they’ve forgotten.
cards.tip: Give clues without ever saying it outright.

cards.title: Waffle Ticket
cards.prompt: A ticket inspector who needs you to explain why your ticket is a waffle.
cards.tip: Take the waffle completely seriously.

cards.title: Discovered It
cards.prompt: An old-fashioned explorer who needs you to agree they just discovered your kitchen.
cards.tip: Name and claim each thing you find.

cards.title: Nervous Volcano
cards.prompt: A volcano who needs you to stop making it nervous.
cards.tip: Rumble softly when worried. Stay very polite.

cards.title: Coach of Napping
cards.prompt: A coach who needs you to give one hundred and ten percent at napping.
cards.tip: Coach it hard, but whisper. Athletes are resting.

cards.title: Sign In, Please
cards.prompt: A security guard who needs you to sign in, even though it’s your house.
cards.tip: Follow the rules exactly. Apologise for nothing.

cards.title: Needy Houseplant
cards.prompt: A houseplant who needs you to move it six inches to the left.
cards.tip: Every new spot is almost right.

cards.title: This Lovely Box
cards.prompt: A real-estate agent who needs you to buy this cardboard box today.
cards.tip: Name one feature of the box per line.

cards.title: Yes, And
cards.prompt: Every line starts with “Yes, and…” then adds one new detail.
cards.tip: Accept what they said before you add to it.

cards.title: Nature Documentary
cards.prompt: Describe yourselves in a hushed nature-documentary voice, as a rare species.
cards.tip: Be amazed by small habits. Keep it hushed.

cards.title: Whispered Golf
cards.prompt: Commentate on each other in whispers, like the final hole of golf.
cards.tip: Make tiny choices sound like enormous moments.

cards.title: Name It Exactly
cards.prompt: Never say “thing” or “stuff.” Every object gets an exact name.
cards.tip: Not “a sandwich”: “a cold egg sandwich, crusts off.”

cards.title: Very Important Partner
cards.prompt: Everyone treats the Partner like the most important person in the world.
cards.tip: Partner: accept the attention. Don’t brush it off.

cards.title: Borrow a Word
cards.prompt: Start each line with any word the other person just said.
cards.tip: Take the word you like best, not the easiest.
cards.cue: Start with one of their words

cards.title: Catch the Mood
cards.prompt: Each line picks up the other person’s feeling and makes it bigger.
cards.tip: Name the feeling once, then let it grow.
cards.cue: Catch the feeling, make it bigger

cards.title: First Time Ever
cards.prompt: Everything in this scene is happening for the very first time in history.
cards.tip: Be amazed by ordinary things, like doors.

cards.title: Questions Only
cards.prompt: Every line must be a question. The scene still has to move.
cards.tip: A question can smuggle in a new fact.

cards.title: Last Word First
cards.prompt: Start each line with the last word the other person said.
cards.tip: You can’t plan ahead. You have to listen.

cards.title: Three Words
cards.prompt: Every line is exactly three words long.
cards.tip: Three words can still accept and build.

cards.title: Film Noir
cards.prompt: Talk like a gloomy old detective film. Short sentences. Rain. Regret.
cards.tip: Describe ordinary things as if they’re hiding something.

cards.title: Polite Fury
cards.prompt: Everyone is furious and perfectly polite. Nobody raises their voice.
cards.tip: Be furious at the situation, never at each other.

cards.title: After You
cards.prompt: Both of you keep trying to be the least important person here.
cards.tip: Lower yourself kindly. Lift the other person up.

cards.title: Alphabet Scene
cards.prompt: Each line starts with the next letter of the alphabet, starting from A.
cards.tip: Names and sounds count. “X-ray!” is fine.

cards.title: Bring It Back
cards.prompt: Every line must mention something already said in this scene.
cards.tip: The oldest detail makes the best callback.

cards.title: Indoor Rain
cards.prompt: It starts raining indoors. Just a light, steady drizzle.
cards.tip: Don’t stop the scene. Carry on, wetter.

cards.title: Half Gravity
cards.prompt: Gravity is suddenly half as strong as it was a moment ago.
cards.tip: Describe it out loud. Nobody needs to move.

cards.title: Best News Ever
cards.prompt: Someone here has just had the best news of their life.
cards.tip: Decide who in your very next line.

cards.title: Very Sleepy
cards.prompt: Everyone is suddenly, deeply sleepy.
cards.tip: Keep wanting what you wanted, just slower.

cards.title: Secret Champion
cards.prompt: One of you is secretly a world champion at something very small.
cards.tip: Name the tiny sport. Let it help.

cards.title: Demoted
cards.prompt: Whoever was in charge has just been demoted. The other is promoted.
cards.tip: Play the new pecking order immediately.

cards.title: Loose Goose
cards.prompt: A goose has got in. Nobody knows whose it is.
cards.tip: Someone on deck can walk on as the owner.

cards.title: Power Cut
cards.prompt: The lights go out. Somebody has a very small torch.
cards.tip: Describe what you can hear and feel.

cards.title: Forgotten Birthday
cards.prompt: It is somebody’s birthday today, and everyone forgot.
cards.tip: Decide whose, fast. Then make it up to them.

cards.title: Inspector Incoming
cards.prompt: A health inspector arrives in exactly one minute.
cards.tip: Hide or fix one thing, out loud.

cards.title: Moving the Whole Time
cards.prompt: This whole place has been on a moving train all along.
cards.tip: Agree where the train is going.

cards.title: Warm Parcel
cards.prompt: A parcel arrives for the Partner. It’s warm and smells of cinnamon.
cards.tip: Open it in words. Name what’s inside.

cards.title: One-Word Story
cards.prompt: Tell a story one word each, around the group. End with “The end.”
cards.tip: Say the first word you can picture.

seeds: The Suitcase That Wanted to Stay Home
The Town Where It Only Rained on Tuesdays
The Last Sock in the Drawer

cards.title: Good News, Bad News
cards.prompt: Swing a story between “Fortunately” and “Unfortunately,” one line each.
cards.tip: “Unfortunately” complicates. It never deletes the last fact.

seeds: We left the house on time.
The map says there’s a shortcut.
The car radio only plays one song.
The dog learned to open doors.

cards.title: The Expert
cards.prompt: One player is the world’s leading expert. Everyone else asks questions.
cards.tip: No wrong answers. Only answers said with confidence.

seeds: the invention of the left turn
the secret life of traffic cones

cards.title: Emotional Forecast
cards.prompt: Everyone says the same ordinary line, each in a new feeling.
cards.tip: The words stay the same. Only the feeling changes.

cards.title: Half-Life
cards.prompt: Tell a tiny story in 60 seconds. Retell it in 30, then 15.
cards.tip: Keep the best moments. Drop everything else.

seeds: The last seat on the bus

cards.title: Story Spine
cards.prompt: Build a story together, one step of the spine per player.
cards.tip: Created by Kenn Adams. Follow the cues in order.

seeds: a town with one traffic light

cards.title: Three Things
cards.prompt: Name a category. The next player lists three of them, fast.
cards.tip: Speed beats accuracy. Celebrate every answer, even wrong ones.

seeds: things a pirate keeps in a lunchbox
rules at a dragon’s birthday party

cards.title: New Choice
cards.prompt: One player tells a story. Say “New choice” to swap the last detail.
cards.tip: Teller: replace the detail instantly. Never argue with it.

seeds: My first day as a lighthouse keeper
The time I won the county fair
My job at the moon’s only café
How I lost the family recipe

cards.title: Gibberish Interpreter
cards.prompt: One player speaks an invented language. The next one translates, confidently.
cards.tip: Translate the tone you hear, not the sounds.

seeds: a visiting chef explains their famous dish
a royal visitor gives a speech about soup
an inventor presents a new kind of umbrella
an explorer describes their worst campsite
a champion knitter accepts an award
a tourist asks for directions to the beach

cards.title: Sound Effects Story
cards.prompt: One player tells a story. Everyone else provides every sound effect.
cards.tip: Teller: leave a little gap for each sound.

seeds: A stormy night on a fishing boat
Breakfast in a very busy kitchen
The longest car wash in the world
A thunderstorm at a petting zoo
A rocket launch from the back garden
The squeakiest night at the museum

cards.title: Advice Line
cards.prompt: A late-night radio advice hour. Callers bring tiny problems. Hosts answer seriously.
cards.tip: Treat the smallest problem like a life decision.

seeds: I can’t choose a favourite spoon.
I said “you too” when the waiter said “enjoy your meal.”
My neighbour’s rooster crows at 3 a.m.
I always pick the slowest queue.

cards.title: Human Machine
cards.prompt: One by one, join a machine with a repeating sound and movement.
cards.tip: Connect to someone already moving. Keep your rhythm.

seeds: a machine that walks the dog

cards.title: World’s Largest Spoon
cards.prompt: You pull up beside the World’s Largest Spoon. It gleams, and it’s slightly bent.
cards.tip: Bring the souvenir in early. Let it matter.

cards.title: The Great Ball of String
cards.prompt: You reach the biggest ball of string on Earth. It hums in the wind.
cards.tip: Decide why you came all this way.

cards.title: Leaning Water Tower
cards.prompt: You arrive at the Leaning Water Tower. The tourists all lean the other way.
cards.tip: Bring back the souvenir in your first three lines.

cards.title: Summit of Mount Average
cards.prompt: You reach the summit of Mount Average. It is exactly as tall as expected.
cards.tip: Make the souvenir the reason the climb was worth it.

cards.title: Sandwich Hall of Fame
cards.prompt: The doors open on the Sandwich Hall of Fame. It smells like a picnic.
cards.tip: Name one famous sandwich and why it’s famous.

cards.title: The Moon’s Gift Shop
cards.prompt: The rocket door opens on the Moon’s only gift shop. A little bell jingles.
cards.tip: The souvenir might be for sale here. Or priceless.
